name: United States (federal)

response.rule_text: 20 working days to respond; 'unusual circumstances' add 10 working days; the clock can be tolled once for clarification and for fee questions. Expedited processing is decided within 10 calendar days.

fees.labor_rule: Search, review (commercial requesters only) and duplication. Media, educational and non-commercial scientific requesters pay no search fees and get 100 free pages.
fees.copy_rule: Nothing is charged when the total is $25 or less.
fees.waiver_rule: Fee waiver when disclosure is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government and is not primarily commercial.
fees.late_penalty: An agency that misses the statutory deadline may not charge search fees (or duplication fees for media and educational requesters). The rule comes from the OPEN Government Act of 2007, 5 U.S.C. 552(a)(4)(A)(viii); the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 narrowed its exceptions to unusual circumstances noticed in time (and over 5,000 pages, case by case).

appeal.body: Agency appeal office, then OGIS mediation or federal district court
appeal.rule_text: At least 90 days to file an administrative appeal; the agency has 20 working days to decide. OGIS mediation is non-binding. Suit in federal district court; constructive exhaustion once the deadline is missed.

format_rule: Records are provided in any form or format requested if readily reproducible in that form.
notes: Executive-branch agencies only: not Congress, the courts, the President's immediate staff, or state and local bodies. The $25 no-charge floor, the 10-calendar-day expedited decision, the 100 free pages for media and educational requesters, OGIS mediation and the late-fee rule are stated on foia.gov/faq.html (in sources). A missed deadline lets the requester treat remedies as exhausted and sue; whether it counts as a denial is not stated here.
